header.title: AI-native portfolio workspace
header.subtitle: A design-engineered portfolio where hiring teams can browse work normally or ask focused questions through a grounded realtime assistant. Built with Next.js, WebRTC, OpenAI Realtime, and Slice.

ai.summary: Uris Design is an AI-native portfolio workspace that lets hiring teams browse projects normally or ask focused questions through Vi, a grounded realtime assistant that can retrieve portfolio context and navigate to relevant evidence.
ai.tagline: A design-engineered portfolio where conversation is an optional discovery and navigation layer, not a chat overlay.
context: The product addresses a hiring-review problem: reviewers arrive with specific questions about design systems, AI, realtime work, or frontend depth, while conventional portfolios make them search across disconnected pages.
Visitors can browse projects, skills, and contact information directly. Vi is optional and helps when someone wants a shortcut, an explanation, or the relevant evidence opened in the workspace.

The assistant is grounded in structured portfolio and skills data. Its authority is intentionally narrow: it can retrieve project or skills details, open known portfolio views, list projects, and update selected UI settings. It cannot take arbitrary browser or external actions.
Voice is optional and interruptible. Text and conventional navigation remain first-class paths so the experience does not depend on microphone access or a voice conversation.

Next.js supports performance in two ways: App Router and static project routes keep the content experience fast by default, while next/image turns high-resolution source imagery, often several megabytes at 3x or 4x resolution, into optimized delivery assets. This matters because visual case-study media is a major part of the portfolio experience.

Realtime state is separated across connection lifecycle, assistant speech, response history, streaming transcripts, tool calls, and UI callbacks so live interaction remains predictable and extensible.
Slice is Uris's UI and browser runtime library. This portfolio is a real product proving ground for its theme, layout, notification, media-device, and WebRTC primitives.

Uris owned the product concept, information architecture, interaction model, UI system, frontend architecture, realtime integration, state model, shared API boundary, and the Slice primitives the workspace uses.
emphasize: The portfolio as an interactive workspace, not a brochure or chat overlay
Conversation as optional discovery and navigation, alongside conventional browsing
Grounded assistant behavior and a deliberately bounded tool surface
Performance-conscious Next.js delivery for both static content and image-heavy case studies
Design-engineering depth across product thinking, interaction design, frontend architecture, and realtime state
Slice as a real UI and browser runtime foundation, not just a styling layer
avoid: Reducing the project to a chatbot demo or treating it as voice-only
Treating it as only a design exercise or only a frontend implementation
Implying the assistant can perform arbitrary site, browser, or external actions
Claiming user, conversion, engagement, or accessibility outcomes that are not evidenced
suggestedQuestions: What makes this different from a typical portfolio or chat widget?
How does Vi stay grounded in the portfolio content?
What can the assistant do, and what is it intentionally not allowed to do?
How does Next.js keep a visual, image-heavy portfolio fast?
Why use WebRTC for this experience?

limitations: Do not imply arbitrary tool execution beyond project details, skills, known views, project listing, and selected UI settings
Do not imply that voice is required to use the portfolio
Do not describe the assistant as autonomous or able to manipulate the browser freely
Do not invent performance, accessibility, adoption, or hiring outcomes
